sections.heading: Gradient flow.
sections.text:
We study the dynamics of the continuous time limit of gradient descent, the gradient flow. Although this analysis does not capture discrete-time effects, adaptive step sizes, or stochasticity, it nevertheless captures the principal behavior of first-order optimization and provides useful insight into the training process. sections.heading: 3.1 Logistic loss
sections.text: We consider a binary classification setting, mirroring standard transformer training where the final representation is optimized with cross-entropy (i.e., logistic loss in the binary case). sections.heading: Assumption 3.1 .
sections.text: The parameters 𝐕 , 𝒂 \mathbf{V},\bm{a} are initialized such that 𝒂 ⁡ ( 0 ) = 0 \bm{a}(0)=0 and 𝒖 0 ​ ( 0 ) > 𝒖 1 ​ ( 0 ) > … > 𝒖 p − 1 ​ ( 0 ) \bm{u}_{0}(0)>\bm{u}_{1}(0)>\ldots>\bm{u}_{p-1}(0) for the projection 𝒖 = 𝐕 ⊤ ​ 𝜷 ∗ \bm{u}=\mathbf{V}^{\top}\bm{\beta}_{*} . This assumption is mild. The condition 𝒂 ⁡ ( 0 ) = 0 \bm{a}(0)=0 implies 𝒔 ⁡ ( 0 ) \bm{s}(0) is uniform, which is consistent with standard practice. Without loss of generality, we assume the coordinates of 𝒖 ⁡ ( 0 ) \bm{u}(0) are ordered by re-indexing. The strict ordering holds almost surely under generic random initialization and can be relaxed if needed. We now show that gradient flow preserves this ordering and induces repulsion between coordinates.

sections.heading: Theorem 3.2 .
sections.text: Consider gradient flow on the loss ( 5 ) under the initialization in Assumption 3.1 . Then, for all t > 0 t>0 , (a) Order preservation. The order of both the projections 𝒖 i ​ ( t ) \bm{u}_{i}(t) and attention scores 𝒔 i ​ ( t ) \bm{s}_{i}(t) is preserved 𝒖 0 ​ ( t ) \displaystyle\bm{u}_{0}(t) > 𝒖 1 ​ ( t ) > … > 𝒖 p − 1 ​ ( t ) , \displaystyle>\bm{u}_{1}(t)>\ldots>\bm{u}_{p-1}(t), 𝒔 0 ​ ( t ) \displaystyle\bm{s}_{0}(t) > 𝒔 1 ​ ( t ) > … > 𝒔 p − 1 ​ ( t ) . \displaystyle>\bm{s}_{1}(t)>\ldots>\bm{s}_{p-1}(t). (b) Repulsion. Pairwise gaps between value projections grow over time: for any i ≠ j i\neq j and any t + > t ⩾ 0 t_{+}>t\geqslant 0 , ( 𝒖 i ​ ( t + ) − 𝒖 j ​ ( t + ) ) > ( 𝒖 i ​ ( t ) − 𝒖 j ​ ( t ) ) . \displaystyle\left(\bm{u}_{i}(t_{+})-\bm{u}_{j}(t_{+})\right)>\left(\bm{u}_{i}(t)-\bm{u}_{j}(t)\right). Theorem 3.2 first establishes a no-crossing property: the coordinate ordering is preserved along the trajectory. To prove this, we introduce the Lyapunov potential Φ i ​ j = − ( e − 𝒂 i − e − 𝒂 j ) ​ ( 𝒖 i − 𝒖 j ) \Phi_{ij}=-\left(e^{-{\bm{a}}_{i}}-e^{-{\bm{a}}_{j}}\right)\left(\bm{u}_{i}-\bm{u}_{j}\right) for i ≠ j ∈ [ p ] i\neq j\in[p] . The derivative of potential is positive, d ​ Φ i ​ j > 0 \textup{{d}}{\Phi_{ij}}>0 , hence the relative ordering between the scores and projections is preserved. In particular, Φ i ​ j ​ ( t ) > 0 \Phi_{ij}(t)>0 , for all t > 0 t>0 , hence the co-ordinates never cross and the initial order remains conserved. Second, the gradient flow exhibits repulsion among the coordinates of 𝒖 \bm{u} : for i < j i , we have d ​ ( 𝒖 i − 𝒖 j ) > 0 \textup{{d}}{(\bm{u}_{i}-\bm{u}_{j})}>0 , driven by the preserved ordering of the attention scores. Together, these properties highlight the polarizing nature of the gradient field in the value–softmax model. Figure 2 : Experimental verification of Theorem 3.3 using logistic loss. The plot shows the evolution of attention scores σ ⁡ ( a ) \sigma(a) and value projections u u over time. As predicted, the attention scores converge to a one-hot vector (blue line goes to 1, others to 0) and the value projections u u diverge, preserving their order.

sections.heading: No-crossing property.
sections.text: Now that we have established the gradient flow dynamics of the value-softmax model over the logistic loss function, we will analyze some properties of the dynamics. We will now give a lemma which highlights the ”no-crossing” property of the dynamics. The lemma proceeds by studing the differences between co-ordinates of the projection vector 𝒖 \bm{u} and 𝒂 \bm{a} . See 3.2
